output.reason: A 68-year-old with two weeks of worsening bilateral ankle swelling and new two-night orthopnea requiring sitting up to breathe suggests decompensating heart failure needing immediate emergency assessment with oxygen saturation, imaging and cardiac evaluation.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. New trouble breathing when lying flat, together with worsening swelling in both ankles, can mean fluid building up from a heart or lung problem that needs same-hour tests and treatment. Have someone drive you rather than driving yourself. If breathing becomes severe, you have chest pain, or you faint, call 911 immediately.
differential: Decompensated heart failure with pulmonary congestion
Other cause of fluid overload (e.g. kidney or liver disease)

redFlags.concern: Orthopnea — must sit up to breathe
redFlags.quote: The last two nights I've had to sit up to breathe because lying flat makes me short of breath
Both my ankles have been swelling for a couple weeks and it's gotten worse

output.vitalSigns: No vital signs reported; oxygen saturation, heart rate and blood pressure are unknown and it is unknown whether any measurement occurred.
